title: Velocity at t=2.0s
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the instantaneous velocity of rod MN at t=2.0s as 0.80 m/s using the given current and the relationship v = IR/(Bl).

title: Power at t=4.0s
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the instantaneous power of force F at t=4.0s as 3.1 W using P = Fv, with correct F and v at that instant.

title: Work done by F
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the total work done by force F on rod MN during 0~3.0s as 2.7 J using energy conservation.

title: EMF and Ohm's Law
description: Important: Applies the correct motional EMF formula (E = 2Blv) for the two moving rods and uses Ohm's Law (I = E / total resistance) to relate current and velocity.

title: Force Analysis
description: Important: Applies Newton's second law to the system (or individual rods) correctly, accounting for gravity, the external force F, and the Ampere forces on both rods.

title: Energy Conservation Setup
description: Important: Sets up the energy conservation equation: Work by F = change in gravitational PE + change in kinetic energy of both rods + total Joule heat in circuit.

title: Kinematics for Distance
description: Optional: Correctly determines the distance h rod MN moves in 3.0s using kinematics (h = v²/(2a) or equivalent), given the uniform acceleration.

title: Total Heat Calculation
description: Optional: Recognizes that the heat generated in MN is half the total circuit heat (Q_all = 2 * Q_MN) because the rods have equal resistance.

title: Incorrect EMF Formula
description: Pitfall: Uses E = Blv for only one rod, forgetting the series contribution from the second rod, leading to a factor-of-two error in velocity or current.

title: Sign Error in Forces
description: Pitfall: Misplaces the sign/direction of the Ampere force(s) or the net force in Newton's second law, leading to an incorrect value for F or acceleration.
